newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU firms showed no wheat contracts for Africa - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: EU firms showed no wheat contracts for Africa - ONIC.

text.p: Exporters who had applied for long-term licences to sell EU wheat to a target group of African nations did not show proof of contract by the 1400 GMT deadline on Friday, France's grain office said.
Traders had applied for licences valid until June 30, 1997 under the so-called article nine that requires traders to show proof of sale to get their refunds.
The licences carried a special refund of 12 Ecus per tonne until December and 19 Ecus from December onwards.
Under the long-term scheme traders had applied for licences to export between 350,000 and one million tonnes of wheat.

On Wednesday, ONIC's director general Alain Moulinier had explained that traders had no incentive to export wheat to these destinations because current EU wheat export rebates exceeded the level of the special refunds set for Africa.
When the EU set the special refunds, world wheat prices were still firm. But since then the EU has stepped up its refund on wheat exports to keep pace with falling world prices.
A rally in U.S. wheat futures on Tuesday and Wednesday, however, momentarily eased pressure for lower EU wheat export subsidies.
On Thursday, the Commission lowered the refund offered on wheat exports to 15.97 Ecus per tonne from 22.35 Ecus.
